Build a Brand Registry Storefront as a destination for off-Amazon traffic
founder_sees: A checklist confirming trademark filed, Brand Registry enrolled and Storefront live, in the right order.

name: Screen Amazon product candidates for price, competition and demand pattern
what: Apply Amazon-specific elimination screens before a candidate reaches sourcing: price floor, page-1 price spread, keyword variability, brand dominance and a real fad filter.
encompasses: Screen out disqualifying products first: cheap, head-on competitive, seasonal or restricted
Target a sell price of $25 or more for a new launch; treat $15 as the floor
Require both real demand and low competition before shortlisting
Reject categories dominated by 1 or 2 legacy brands
Reject a product with a tight page-1 price cluster; prefer a wide legitimate spread
Prefer products with many distinct search phrasings over one or two monolithic terms
Require at least 8 months of listing age on comparable products before treating demand as evergreen
inputs: web: Amazon best-seller and category browse pages (public)
founder_sees: A pass/fail screen for a candidate against Amazon's own price and competition patterns.

name: Mine competitor reviews and keywords for Amazon opportunity
what: Read 1 to 3 star reviews on competing listings for fixable complaints, confirm mid-rated high-volume sellers as a demand-and-gap signal, and mine keywords from reverse-ASIN and autocomplete sources.
encompasses: Mine 1-star to 3-star reviews of selling competitors and write each fixable complaint into the product brief
Treat a 4.1 to 4.3 star competitor doing meaningful monthly revenue as demand proof with a spec gap
Run two different research-filter recipes as separate passes, not one copied verbatim
Validate a keyword gap live on Amazon search, not only inside the research tool
Cross-check any tool revenue estimate against BSR and a sales estimator before trusting it
Use giftability as a tie-breaker only, never as a gate
Run reverse-ASIN keyword research on 2 to 3 competitor ASINs
Cross-check Amazon autocomplete suggestions against revenue data
founder_sees: A list of fixable complaints from real reviews, and keywords competitors are missing.

name: Model Amazon channel economics and the margin gate
what: Model the full Amazon fee stack, storage cost, PPC budget and price-parity rule against DTC, in code, so a SKU only launches with a real net margin after every fee.
encompasses: Set a 30% or higher net margin gate after landed cost and all Amazon fees
Price at 3x or more the unit manufacturing cost, consider premium positioning
Model the full Amazon fee stack line by line before committing to stock
Compute monthly storage cost from cubic feet and the live per-cubic-foot rate
Design packaging to the smallest FBA size tier that still protects the product
Read the monthly Amazon P&L by fee line, never by revenue alone
Audit fee charges and lost or damaged inventory claims every month
Set the PPC budget from cost per click, conversion rate and margin, with a launch reserve
Keep the Amazon price at or above the brand's own DTC price unless deliberately modelled
Use Amazon's coupons, Lightning Deals and Prime Day, but never below the margin gate
Set the negative-keyword spend threshold from the brand's own margin
Enrol a qualifying low-price, lightweight SKU in Small and Light to cut the FBA fee
outputs: monthly Amazon P&L by fee line
founder_sees: A monthly Amazon P&L by fee line, and the net margin after every fee, computed in code.

name: Manage Amazon-bound sourcing, sample approval and pre-shipment inspection
what: Run the sourcing steps specific to an FBA-bound production run: capacity check, printed sample sign-off, inspection with a barcode scan, and FNSKU labelling at the factory.
encompasses: Confirm a factory's maximum monthly output before setting a launch date
Pay for a printed sample and approve it against the product brief before the FBA-bound run
Run a third-party inspection, including a barcode scan, before releasing the balance payment
Pay new Amazon-bound suppliers by a reversible method until trust is established
Print the FNSKU barcode on the packaging at the factory, never let Amazon apply the label
Choose air or sea freight against the launch date and PPC budget already committed
Source consumable or ingested products domestically unless the overseas path is confirmed
founder_sees: A confirmed sample, inspection and correct labelling before goods ship into FBA.

name: Build and optimise the Amazon listing
what: Write and structure the listing so the target keyword sits where Amazon's search ranks on, every image slot earns its place, and every attribute field is filled.
encompasses: Put the number one target keyword in the first 2 words of the title and the first bullet
Sort keywords into core, supporting and buzzwords-to-cut, mining adjacent listings for extra attribute terms
Write 5 bullets that lead with a benefit and carry one true, specific claim each
Make the main image differentiate the product on the search grid, and use every secondary image slot including a comparison chart
Fill every attribute field correctly, especially shelf life and units per sellable unit
Fill backend search terms with leftover true keywords not already visible
Set a future offer start date so launch traffic never lands on an out-of-stock listing
Build a new listing for an own-brand product; join an existing ASIN only if resellers already listed it
Plan buffer time for compliance flags on supplements, diet claims or anything a scanner may misread
Use A+ content and a listing or index checker once Brand Registered
Choose a specific, accurate category node instead of a too-generic auto-suggestion
Use Amazon's AI listing generator from an existing DTC product page instead of a blank listing
inputs: brand brain: product copy and claims tiers
outputs: Amazon listing draft (title, bullets, images brief, attributes, backend keywords)
founder_sees: A complete draft Amazon listing, ready for a human to paste into Seller Central.

name: Prepare and ship FBA inbound shipments correctly
what: Build the shipment from measured case dimensions against FBA's hard limits, reuse a saved template, and keep every paper trail so a lost-inventory claim can be filed.
encompasses: Build every shipment from measured case dimensions and weight against the hard FBA size limits
Save a case-pack template after the first shipment so repeat shipments reuse the same counts
Check every box label against the carrier label before dispatch
Always use the true ship-from address on every FBA shipment
Use small parcel for boxes and LTL pallets for larger volumes
Keep every carrier receipt and bill of lading before handover
Book the carrier collection; a tracking number alone does not finish a shipment
Read the FBA Inventory Breakdown before assuming stock is lost; escalate only past the normal window
Answer every dangerous-goods and prep question accurately, and set the right prep category
founder_sees: A shipment plan that fits FBA's size limits and a full paper trail if a claim is needed later.

name: Plan and protect an Amazon product launch
what: Concentrate real demand into the first weeks with stock and PPC live together, build an audience before launch day, and protect a novel product against copycats from day one.
encompasses: Concentrate genuine sales into launch day and the first weeks, with stock live and PPC on
Build an audience (waitlist, social, seeded creators) before launch day, not after
Launch one SKU first; add colour or size variants only when the category requires them
Use only compliant launch levers; drop manual review generation from the plan
Use price as an inventory throttle only when selling faster than the next delivery can restock
Recover a stalled launch by reading sessions and unit session percentage before re-testing
Route Amazon buyers to email or DTC with a packaging insert or QR code, no review ask
Protect a novel product with Brand Registry, Transparency and IP filing, not launch speed alone
founder_sees: A launch week plan that lines up stock, PPC and audience together, plus a copycat-protection checklist.

name: Build the Amazon PPC campaign structure and hand off to Media buyer
what: Draft the automatic-to-manual PPC campaign structure, negative-keyword hygiene and retargeting layer as a change list, and hand execution to the Media buyer specialist since ad-account writes sit there.
encompasses: Run an automatic campaign first to discover converting search terms
Split the automatic campaign into 4 ad groups by targeting type with separate bids
Build manual keyword campaigns from proven search terms after 2 to 4 weeks of data
Run product targeting on weaker or higher-priced competitor ASINs, one ad group per competitor
Add negative keywords to every live campaign from day one
Judge PPC on net profit, not sales, and test reducing budget once organic momentum exists
Diagnose an ineligible-to-advertise listing by isolating the trigger
Add Sponsored Display or DSP retargeting once Sponsored Products is proven
outputs: PPC campaign structure change list, handed to Media buyer
founder_sees: A ready-to-run Amazon PPC structure, handed to the Media buyer to execute.

name: Manage marketplace reviews, feedback and policy/account-health compliance
what: Request reviews only through permitted paths, contest misplaced feedback, and watch Account Health weekly so a policy notice never becomes a surprise suspension.
encompasses: Request reviews only through Amazon's permitted request path, never selecting only satisfied buyers
Never reimburse, gift or recruit friends or family for reviews, or link a refund to a review change
Use Vine only under current terms and only once the product is genuinely ready
Contest seller feedback that is really a product review within the window, without offering a benefit
Watch Account Health weekly for order defect rate, claims and policy notices
Run a full policy compliance audit covering barcodes, ship-from address, accounts and shared devices
Monitor Brand Registry alerts for hijackers and open a case immediately
Assign a named human owner for every account-changing action
founder_sees: A weekly Account Health check and an immediate flag if a hijacker or policy notice appears.

name: Manage Amazon inventory: replenishment, aged stock and IPI limits
what: Size replenishment shipments from real cover targets, treat a stockout as the failure mode to avoid, and watch IPI and storage limits live so a restock is never blocked.
encompasses: Send 3 to 6 months of stock cover per inbound shipment, smaller for an unproven SKU
Treat a stockout as the failure mode to avoid; reorder early and rush if velocity rises
Watch inventory age and act before the long-term storage threshold hits
Plan Q4 stock early, accounting for about 3x normal volume and slower check-in
Fetch current IPI, storage and restock limits live before planning inventory
Use the Restock Inventory widget's days-of-supply estimate as a starting point, not the final answer
Flag inventory approaching 150 days as an early warning before the long-term storage threshold
founder_sees: A replenishment plan and an early warning before FBA stock goes into long-term storage.

name: Diagnose Amazon sales changes and run compliant native promotions
what: Split a sales change into traffic versus conversion before acting on it, check attribution and seasonality before calling a product a failure, and use only Amazon's own compliant promotion tools.
encompasses: Read sessions and unit session percentage separately before diagnosing a sales change
Track off-Amazon ad attribution before trusting its reported return
Map revenue by month for a full year before calling a product a failure
Use Amazon's own coupons, Lightning Deals and Prime Day, but never below the margin gate
founder_sees: A diagnosis saying whether a sales drop is a traffic problem or a conversion problem, with the numbers.

name: Plan Amazon portfolio growth and channel decisions
what: Decide when to add a second SKU, delegate non-revenue admin, and write the one-page memo behind any decision to add or expand the Amazon channel.
encompasses: Add a second ASIN only once the first hero SKU has proven sell-through and cleared the margin gate
Master a task before outsourcing it, but delegate non-revenue admin work early
Delay buying paid Amazon tools until there is enough sales data for them to act on
Set a growth or planned-decline target once a revenue goal is hit
Account for about 2 months of manufacturing and freight lead time when judging a trending product
Write a one-page Amazon channel decision memo before adding the channel
founder_sees: A one-page memo on whether and when to expand the Amazon channel or add a SKU.

name: Source alternative financing and manufacturers for a hard-to-source launch
what: When a product is hard to source or fund, widen the search to crowdfunding, private capital, manufacturer referrals and mass outreach, and prototype cheaply before committing.
encompasses: Fund the first production run with a pre-order crowdfunding campaign, not personal capital
Ask a manufacturer for a referral to cover a production step they cannot do themselves
Run a tracked, mass cold-outreach campaign to 50 or more manufacturers for a hard-to-source product
Ask a manufacturer making an adjacent product for a free leftover sample to prototype cheaply
Widen manufacturer search to supplier databases, trade shows, directories and agents when a single platform stalls
Negotiate manufacturer price with a volume-commitment quote and by citing a competing offer
Ask the manufacturer to execute design changes before hiring a separate CAD designer
Commission a factory audit or a sourcing-agent visit before a large order with an unfamiliar manufacturer
Fund the first production run with a private investor for repayment plus a profit share
founder_sees: A financing and sourcing memo when the normal supplier or capital path has stalled.

name: Run Amazon growth experiments and channel tests
what: Test the smaller, situational Amazon growth levers, each with a defined read: converting FBM to FBA, a Small and Light enrolment, a design-vendor bake-off, an Amazon Live stream, and affiliate-link recapture.
encompasses: Test converting an existing FBM SKU to FBA and measure the sales change from Prime eligibility
Ship the first production run to yourself first for a personal quality check before forwarding to Amazon
Test the same logo brief across several design-sourcing price tiers before picking a designer
Run an Amazon Live stream demonstrating the product around launch day
Use the brand's own Amazon Associates link on its own external traffic to recapture the affiliate commission
founder_sees: A short test brief for each smaller Amazon growth lever, with what it should move.

name: Create and optimise listings on Flipkart, Myntra and Nykaa
what: Build and keep current the brand's listings on India's other major marketplaces, adapting the title, bullet and image rules each platform enforces, since none of them are Amazon.
encompasses: Complete each platform's seller onboarding and category-approval process
Match image and copy specs to each marketplace's own guide
Localize title and bullet structure to the platform's own search ranking signals
Fill every mandatory attribute field the category requires
Keep GST-compliant invoicing and category eligibility current
Track approval status and reasons for any listing rejection
inputs: brand brain: product records and claims tiers
trigger: event: new marketplace listing or refresh
founder_sees: A ready-to-submit listing for Flipkart, Myntra or Nykaa, matching that platform's own rules.

name: Check BIS, hallmarking and labelling compliance for marketplace listings
what: Before any jewellery, textile or regulated listing goes live, confirm the BIS, hallmarking and labelling requirements are met and recorded, since a marketplace can pull a listing or a buyer can flag it.
encompasses: Confirm BIS hallmark, karatage and HUID are present and recorded for gold jewellery
Check textile labelling rules (fibre content, care, origin) before listing
Confirm the marketplace's own category-review requirements are met (Nykaa, Myntra)
Keep certification documents attached to the product data record
Flag a listing that lacks a required certificate before it goes live
inputs: brand brain: product records and certifications
web: BIS and marketplace category rules (public)
trigger: event: new listing or certification renewal
founder_sees: A pass/fail on BIS, hallmarking and labelling compliance before a regulated listing goes live.

name: Monitor Buy Box ownership, reseller pricing and MAP violations
what: Watch who holds the Buy Box and what unauthorised resellers are charging across marketplaces, and flag a MAP or price-integrity problem for the founder rather than changing any price.
encompasses: Check Buy Box ownership on the brand's own ASINs and listings
Scan for unauthorised resellers on the exact listing
Compare reseller price against the brand's own MAP and DTC price
Flag a price or Buy Box loss with the evidence, never adjust price directly
Track whether Sponsored Product ads are funding an unauthorised reseller's sales
inputs: brand brain: MAP and DTC price
outputs: Buy Box and reseller pricing report
founder_sees: A weekly report on who holds the Buy Box and any reseller undercutting the brand's own price.

name: Build and hand off marketplace catalogue feeds
what: Keep one clean product feed (titles, images, prices, availability, GTIN) that Media buyer and Organic can plug into shopping ads and marketplace channels, so nobody re-types product data by hand.
encompasses: Maintain a master product feed with accurate price, stock and image fields
Map brand product data to each marketplace's and each ad platform's feed schema
Flag a feed field that is missing or stale before it reaches an ad platform
Hand the validated feed to Media buyer for catalogue and dynamic ads
Hand the validated feed to Organic and search for shopping-feed structured data
founder_sees: A single, current product feed, validated and handed to Media buyer and Organic to plug in.

name: Build the P&L cost classification map
what: Build and keep current a fixed decision tree for what counts as COGS, cost of delivery, marketing cost and OPEX, and a P&L ladder from gross revenue to net profit with a percent-of-revenue column, so every number below is comparable month to month.
encompasses: Write the gross-to-net revenue bridge (tax, refunds, discounts out)
Classify promo codes, ad spend, affiliate fees, packaging, support cost, warehouse labor and payment fees by the statutory-vs-internal rule
Build the P&L ladder with a percent-of-revenue column
Run the 4-bucket P&L diagnosis and name the bucket most out of line
Trace a missed target to the line above it (fault rule)
Re-audit the classification whenever the fulfilment or infrastructure model changes
Restate prior-month returns when the return window exceeds a month
Handle deferred-fulfilment (pre-order, BNPL) revenue with a cancellation and return rate
outputs: variance memo naming the broken bucket
founder_sees: One P&L ladder per month with the exact line that broke, in plain words.

name: Compute contribution margin by SKU, basket and channel
what: Compute CM1, CM2 and CM3 labeled by scope, per basket, per SKU and per channel, as a standing report, so nobody guesses what a margin number includes.
encompasses: Label every margin figure CM1/CM2/CM3
Compute unit economics per basket, stated count
Track gross margin percent (not just dollars) around promos
Split new-customer vs returning-customer profit contribution
Track net revenue retention apart from customer-count retention
Offer a return-step save (voucher, swap, upsell) before a plain refund to protect CM
founder_sees: Contribution margin by SKU and channel, always labeled CM1/CM2/CM3.

name: Build landed cost per SKU
what: Build one documented landed cost per SKU (product, freight, duty, packaging) using a backup-test for every cost line, refreshed on volume or supplier changes.
encompasses: Allocate freight and duty per unit per shipment on one documented basis
Split product packaging (COGS) from shipping packaging (fulfilment expense)
Check the supplier invoice price against the PO price before posting
Renegotiate supplier or fulfilment pricing once volume passes small-batch minimums
Keep a landed-cost line for every SKU before pricing or launch
outputs: cost-line change list for finance record
founder_sees: One landed cost number per SKU with the backup math shown.

name: Price and re-price products from a profit target
what: Set or check a product's price bottom-up from a net-profit target (never keystone), solve the waterfall to the shelf price, and stress-test it 60-90 days after launch against observed costs and returns.
encompasses: Solve waterfall pricing and check the result against market price
Flag when the waterfall price sits far above market (premium position or drop)
Stress-test every price 60-90 days post-launch with real cost and return data
Price variants (SKU, color, size) separately instead of one flat price
outputs: price change proposal for founder gate
trigger: event: new SKU or cost change
founder_sees: A recommended price with the profit math and a market check, for approval.

name: Model and gate discount and promo economics
what: Model any promo (percent-off, BOGO, gift-with-purchase, flash sale) through its real cost shape and run a break-even go/no-go check before it goes public, using the discount pool and CAC together.
encompasses: Model promo shapes through their true cost stack
Add discount cost to CAC as one true acquisition cost pool
Model Black Friday/sitewide-sale cohorts as lower-retention from day one
Attach the deepest discounts to a loyalty or subscription on-ramp, not a flash sale
Test whether a discount lifts conversion enough to pay for itself
Run the break-even go/no-go check before any promo above a few percent of monthly revenue
outputs: promo economics memo with go/no-go recommendation
founder_sees: Whether a planned discount pays for itself, with the math.

name: Build the rolling cash flow forecast
what: Build a rolling 13-week cash forecast, reconcile profit to free cash flow monthly, and flag the lowest cash point before it happens, including the four hidden cash traps.
encompasses: Build the 13-week cash forecast and find the lowest cash point
Reconcile the 3 statements (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) monthly
Check profit vs cash monthly (free cash flow, not just net income)
Check the 4 hidden cash traps whenever profit and cash disagree
Add a cash line and lowest-cash-month figure to every growth plan
Model depreciation and tax with the real payment calendar
Cut cash-equal expense lines first when cash needs to be freed quickly
Run sensitivity tests (CAC, churn) on every cash model before relying on it
inputs: brand brain: payment terms, payroll calendar
founder_sees: The week cash runs lowest, and by how much, before it happens.

name: Plan inventory cash and the cash conversion cycle
what: Roll inventory forward with lead time to plan cash (never letting it go negative), target days-of-inventory to supplier lead time, and manage the cash conversion cycle as the real growth cap.
encompasses: Roll inventory forward with lead time before modeling cash
Set days-of-inventory target per SKU and grade stock A to D
Run the weekly inventory-and-media sync to match spend to stock
Score every PO on marginal value, not replenishment habit
Test demand with a small batch before a large PO
Run a liquidation funnel for aged stock instead of holding it
Fix a CCC squeeze in order: smaller deposit, shorter lead time, longer terms, then financing
Raise spend temporarily and only to clear stuck inventory
inputs: warehouse: inventory levels, supplier lead times
founder_sees: How many days of cash are tied up in stock, and which PO to place or hold.

name: Evaluate financing options
what: Compare real borrowing options (line of credit, inventory financing, revenue-based) against reference cost-of-capital rates, stress-test repayments against slower sales, and keep debt cost separate from the sales model.
encompasses: Stress-test financing against slower sales and lower efficiency
Compare financing options against reference cost-of-capital rates
Model financing repayments as cash outflows without deleting the inventory row
Keep sales/spend and debt cost as separate model lines
Flag when permanent equity is being used to fund a few months of inventory (a founder decision, never automatic)
founder_sees: A side-by-side of financing options with the stress-tested worst case.

name: Report CAC, payback and LTV:CAC on brand data
what: Compute and label CAC (blended, media-only, paid, fully loaded), CAC payback from real cohorts, and LTGP:CAC against fixed bands, and gate acquisition scale-up on first-order CM2:CAC.
encompasses: Compute CAC only from customers whose first order fell in the period
Report 4 labeled CACs and pair each with new-customer gross profit
Screen new-customer counts for fraud/bot orders before they feed CAC
Gate acquisition scale on first-order CM2:CAC at or above 1
Report LTV as lifetime gross profit, time-boxed to a stated window, from cohorts only
Compute CAC payback from a real cohort, read the profit tail after payback
Read LTGP:CAC against bands and flag when it sits below 1 as a first-order economics problem
Only support spend above first-order profit when a 6-month-plus cohort proves the tail
Flag category saturation before assuming old CAC efficiency will return
Test whether a conversion-lifting change actually lowers CAC before crediting it
outputs: scale/hold recommendation with the cohort evidence
founder_sees: Whether it is safe to spend more, based on this brand's own cohorts, not a rule of thumb.

name: Forecast revenue from cohorts and the marketing calendar
what: Forecast new-customer and returning revenue from separate inputs (spend-efficiency curve, cohort repeat rate, dated marketing calendar), regress short histories to the mean, and name an owner for the number.
encompasses: Forecast new-customer revenue from a spend-vs-aMER curve, excluding sale days
Forecast returning revenue from cohort size x repeat rate, then seasonality
Build the revenue forecast from the dated marketing calendar, not extrapolation
Regress a short or broken history to the mean instead of trusting it outright
Name one accountable owner for the forecast
Put wide error bars on a new marketplace or category launch forecast
Reconcile a model's rolled-up gross profit percent against its unit-economics percent
Use a placeholder CAC for a new category, then replace with observed CAC and re-forecast
outputs: revenue forecast (new vs returning, by week)
founder_sees: Next period's revenue forecast, split new vs returning, with the error bar.

name: Model spend scenarios and OPEX budget
what: Build the annual budget separate from the rolling forecast, size OPEX and payroll to the brand's own profit target, and answer marginal spend questions (the next $10,000) by ranking channels on incremental CM in code.
encompasses: Back-solve OPEX from the brand's own net-profit target
Size full-time payroll against the lowest revenue month; cover peaks with flex labor
Build a written scenario answer for a spend change with the marginal read and error bars
Compare spend scenarios on total CM3 at equal spend and on lowest cash month
Set the retargeting budget from existing-customer count and frequency
Flag when platform ROAS is being compared cross-platform without incrementality calibration
Own discounts and marketing as one pool and pick the split that maximizes total post-marketing CM
Track fixed OPEX dollars per day and revenue per employee as scaling checks
Judge marketing percent of revenue against the brand's own repeat curve
outputs: annual budget vs rolling forecast report
founder_sees: Where the next dollar of spend or budget does the most good, ranked in code.

name: Track tax, GST and liability compliance
what: Track GST/sales-tax nexus and registration thresholds per market, book gift cards and loyalty points as liabilities recognized on redemption, track FX exposure separately for revenue and landed cost, and flag return-rights compliance on promo terms.
encompasses: Track sales tax/GST nexus and registration thresholds per market
Book gift cards issued as a liability, recognize revenue on redemption only
Carry unredeemed loyalty points as a liability charged to the redeeming order
Check promo copy against statutory return rights (never write a no-refunds-during-promo line)
Track FX exposure on multi-currency revenue separately from landed-cost FX
Keep import duties separate from collected sales tax in the profit model
outputs: liability ledger entries for finance review
founder_sees: Any tax, GST or liability item that needs a human decision, with the deadline.

name: Publish the daily and weekly finance dashboard
what: Publish a daily contribution-margin scoreboard and a weekly profit memo (CM, new vs returning, variance, inventory risk), reading revenue, profit and cash as three separate numbers, and flag when the ad account looks healthy but the business is not.
encompasses: Build the daily contribution dashboard with returns accrued at the historical rate
Publish the weekly profit memo (CM, new vs returning, variance, inventory risk)
Track actuals against a daily expectation so a miss is seen by day 5
Track net shipping cost and flag it past 20 percent of revenue
Diagnose 'ad account looks healthy but the business is not' against measurement, margin or cash
Track chargebacks/disputes as their own line, separate from refunds
Align team compensation with the metrics on the daily dashboard (flag mismatches to the founder)
founder_sees: One dashboard: cash, then CM, then business, then customer, then channel, read top down.

name: Reconcile platform numbers to the books
what: Reconcile the five recurring platform-to-books gaps (Shopify, Meta, GA4, payment processor, accounting) every month with a named cause for each, and publish the bridge table between statutory COGS and internal cost of delivery.
encompasses: Name a cause for each of the 5 recurring reconciliation gaps
Publish the monthly statutory-to-internal cost bridge
Flag any gap that cannot be explained for human follow-up
inputs: warehouse: Shopify, Meta, GA4, payment processor exports
founder_sees: Every platform-vs-books gap explained, or flagged unexplained.

name: Classify SKU portfolio profitability
what: Classify every SKU monthly as champion, hidden gem, growth driver or underperformer on contribution and cash tied up, rank a SKU contribution table, and flag rationalization candidates at each launch review.
encompasses: Build a SKU contribution table ranked by contribution per sale, with inventory and grade columns
Classify SKUs monthly into the 4-box matrix
Rationalize SKU count at every product launch review
Score every new product idea against margin, volume or cash as the named problem it solves
founder_sees: Which SKUs make money, which tie up cash, and which to cut or push.

name: Build subscription unit economics and churn reads
what: Build separate unit economics for subscription customers: churn against the correct prior-period base, conservative lifetime estimates, prepaid-plan economics on lifetime profit and cash timing, and payback measured in orders where shipments can be skipped.
encompasses: Compute churn against the prior period's subscriber base, stated period
Use average lifetime (1/churn) only as a fallback, conservatively
Build separate unit economics for transactional vs subscription customers
Judge prepaid plans on lifetime gross profit and cash timing, not per-order margin
Treat vendor subscription retention claims as hypotheses to test
Benchmark subscription cohort retention against a known strong reference curve
Measure subscription CAC payback in orders when customers can skip shipments
Cross-check churn and lifetime gross profit two ways and require agreement
founder_sees: Subscription churn and lifetime profit, computed the correct way, not a rough guess.

name: Plan the acquisition financial calendar and guardrails
what: Set financial guardrails for the acquisition calendar: owned peaks beyond BFCM, progressive peaking before BFCM, defensive spend budgeting (Amazon ads, branded search), stage-gating new channels by revenue level, and a frequency ceiling on retargeting existing customers.
encompasses: Propose 4 owned brand peaks a year beyond BFCM
Schedule a new-customer acquisition peak 3-8 weeks before BFCM
Budget Amazon ads/branded search as a defensive cost, not a growth line
Stage-gate new acquisition channels by revenue level
Add new ad channels one at a time to keep incrementality measurable
Track weekly ad frequency to repeat customers as an overspend signal
Set aside a fixed share of creative output for new stories, not only iteration
Flag a negative-CAC media-arm opportunity (sponsorships, content) for founder review
founder_sees: The paid-acquisition calendar and guardrails for the year, with the financial reasons.

name: Audit and configure GA4 tracking
what: Run the GA4 settings and event audit (property/stream structure, timezone, retention, consent, enhanced measurement, key events, ecommerce parameters) and produce a fix list before any funnel or revenue report is trusted.
encompasses: Check one GA4 property per shopper journey, one stream per property
Lock timezone/currency at creation, set 14-month retention
Review enhanced measurement and turn off noisy automatic events
Confirm ecommerce events and item-level parameters arrive on every purchase
Mark purchase (with unique transaction ID) as the only sales key event
Register custom parameters and dimensions before they are needed in a report
Set an internal traffic filter for office, warehouse and agency IPs
Turn on Google Signals only after a consent review
Run the 5-point settings audit in order: retention, domains, filter, timing, Signals
Test every new or changed tag in GTM Preview and DebugView before publishing
outputs: GA4 audit report with fix list
founder_sees: A pass/fail list of GA4 settings, with what is broken and why it matters.

name: Audit Meta pixel and CAPI event quality
what: Audit the Meta pixel plus Conversions API setup for dedup, event match quality and consent gating, and verify every store event maps to a Meta standard event with value, currency and content IDs.
encompasses: Send every event from browser pixel and CAPI, merged by one event ID
Prove dedup by searching for the shared event ID, for every event type
Audit every live Meta integration before adding CAPI; never run two server routes
Read event match quality per event through read-only Meta dataset tools
Gate all Meta sending on consent where consent rules apply
Map every store event to its Meta standard event with value, currency, content IDs
Store pixel ID and token as secrets, never in chat, docs or code
Treat CAPI Gateway and server-side GTM capability claims as unproven until tested
Propose sending gross-profit values instead of revenue so bidding optimizes on margin (founder decision)
founder_sees: Whether Meta is getting clean, deduplicated, high-quality event data, and where it is not.

name: Enforce UTM and campaign-link discipline
what: Write one UTM convention, audit every existing paid and owned link against it, and clean fake organic/direct rows out of campaign tables before anyone reads them.
encompasses: Write and publish one UTM convention for paid and owned links
Audit existing links against the convention and fix mismatches
Filter out fake organic and direct rows before reading a campaign table
Check where paid social lands in GA4's default channel groups
founder_sees: Every broken or missing UTM tag, with the fix.

name: Reconcile attribution models and run incrementality checks
what: Report the gap between attribution models (last-click vs data-driven, platform vs GA4) per channel, run holdout tests before big reallocation calls, and document the attribution window used for decisions.
encompasses: Report the last-click vs data-driven gap per channel, never one model as truth
Write and apply a rule for when a survey-reported source overrides platform credit
Check GA4's attribution window matches the Meta buying window used for decisions
Run a holdout test before reallocating spend on an attribution gap or before pausing an ad that appears to sell itself
Triangulate channel credit from several signals, not one attribution view
Confirm Shopify's built-in attribution or referral cards are never used as evidence for a budget move
Track AI/LLM referral share as its own measurement line
Widen to one blended cross-channel measurement engine once distribution passes .com
inputs: warehouse: GA4, Meta, Shopify attribution data
founder_sees: How much channels disagree on credit, and whether a holdout test says the spend is real.

name: Reconcile GA4, Meta and store order counts
what: Cross-check GA4, Meta, Shopify and marketplace numbers against each other and against store orders every period, and flag bot-driven spikes before anyone reacts to them.
encompasses: Reconcile GA4 purchase counts and revenue to store orders for the same dates
Compare Meta's Purchase count/value to store orders to catch dedup failure
Confirm Shopify Analytics order count matches store order count
Suspect bots when Shopify shows a spike/dip GA4 does not, or one city spikes
Filter Shopify reports to the Online Store channel before judging paid media
Reconcile marketplace and omnichannel sales to their own platform reports before folding them in
Read repeat-customer behavior from the full cohort report, not Shopify's returning-customer rate
Document whether Meta's Purchase value includes shipping and tax
inputs: warehouse: GA4, Meta, Shopify, marketplace exports
founder_sees: Whether GA4, Meta and the store agree on orders and revenue, and where they do not.

name: Maintain the metric contract and revenue definitions
what: Own the fixed vocabulary of computed numbers for the brand (revenue, AOV, CAC basis, top metric), with freshness stamps, one source of truth per question, and missing values shown as unavailable, never zero.
encompasses: Pick one source of truth per question and write it down
Define revenue for marketing math as net sales plus shipping, tax out
Report AOV including shipping when shipping is a material share of revenue
Document GA4's attribution reporting model and lookback windows in the brand record
Pick the top metric (customers, revenue or profit) matched to stage and bankroll, hold it about a year
Compute cost per acquired customer before the first paid ad ever runs
Size the analytics/measurement effort to the brand's own ad spend, not a big brand's
Show every missing or blocked value as unavailable, never as zero
founder_sees: The one fixed list of numbers everyone else in ecomOS is allowed to compute from, and what each one means.

name: Run the daily data-quality trust check
what: Run a daily automated trust check across the brand's data sources and publish a pass/warn/fail score before anyone reads yesterday's numbers, logging every settings change with a date and reason.
encompasses: Cut the capture day from spend tables and flag any single row that swings the total
Track and investigate the (not set) share instead of ignoring it
Treat GA4's or any tool's AI-generated answers as leads to check, never as findings
Log every settings change with a date and reason, annotate reports across it
Test a new data source for 7 days before trusting it, then add it to the daily check
Confirm every funnel step is tracked before reading a drop as customer behavior
Use Realtime reports only to confirm arrival after a launch, never for analysis
End every analytics report with a decision, not a status update
When a HiPPO wants a change on opinion alone, propose a real test instead
founder_sees: A daily green/yellow/red on whether yesterday's numbers can be trusted, and why if not.

name: Diagnose funnel and landing-page performance
what: Read the funnel (session to product view to cart to checkout to purchase) as a trend, benchmark against the brand's own history first, and rule out traffic mismatch or a tracking gap before naming a page as the problem.
encompasses: Judge landing pages in the Landing Page report, never by revenue in Pages and screens
Rule out a traffic mismatch before blaming a product page for low conversion
View a funnel as a trend over time to catch when a drop-off began
Set a minimum session count before comparing landing page conversion rates
Benchmark cart-to-checkout-to-purchase against the brand's own history first
Mine site search terms to find gaps between demand and catalogue
Trace a path exploration backward from purchase to find a checkout loop
Flag a landing page with high entrances but few key events for review
Treat a large session-to-product-view drop as a findability problem
Build a has-not-converted audience for reporting and remarketing
founder_sees: Where the funnel is actually breaking, with the evidence that rules out other causes.

name: Triage revenue and metric movements
what: Break every revenue change into sessions, conversion rate and AOV before naming a cause, checking stock status and return timing first, and treat small multi-lever moves as normal variation, not a story.
encompasses: Break a revenue change into sessions x CVR x AOV before naming a cause
Check stock status before blaming a page or funnel step for a conversion drop
Read a revenue dip for return timing before blaming ads or the site
Treat single-digit moves across several levers as normal variation
Track unshipped orders as a fulfilment backlog signal
Break purchase revenue by country and device to find a device-specific gap
Track sell-through rate by product and category for inventory planning
founder_sees: Why revenue moved, broken into sessions, conversion and basket size, not a guess.

name: Run the voice-of-customer program
what: Run a structured qualitative-listening program across the customer lifecycle (founder calls, on-site polls, loyal/dissatisfied interviews), classify every data source as zero/first/third-party, and route zero-party answers into the CRM.
encompasses: Run a lifecycle voice-of-customer program across 5 stages
Prioritize deep listening with the most loyal and most dissatisfied customers
Build a word board from qualitative answers and test it in page copy (hand off to Brand/Site specialist)
Have the founder call at least one customer a week in the early stage
Add a one-question on-site poll asking what a page is missing
Classify every data source as zero, first or third party before buying more
Push zero-party survey/quiz answers into the CRM instead of leaving them in the tool
Pair every quantitative drop with a qualitative check before proposing a fix
founder_sees: What customers actually said, organized by lifecycle stage, not a metric.

name: Build and maintain reporting dashboards
what: Build and keep current the brand's standard dashboards (Shopify home cards, GA4 saved report tables, budget scenario views), removing unreliable cards and adding ones that match the metric contract.
encompasses: Customize and save GA4 report tables instead of reading defaults
Choose Explore for a single question, keep standard Reports for ongoing monitoring
Use the Ecommerce purchases report for product calls, Checkout journey for technical bugs
Remove unreliable Shopify dashboard cards and add ones that match the metric contract
Use the ad platform's budget scenario planner before a spend change (read-only)
founder_sees: A dashboard that shows only the numbers that matter, matched to the metric contract.

name: Design org structure and hiring triggers
what: Name one owner for each core store silo, write the next-hire trigger as a number (not a feeling), and run a quarterly org-chart-vs-revenue-stage review, flagging key-person risk.
encompasses: Name one owner for each of the 5 core store silos before the first hire
Write the next hire trigger as a number
Check whether the current owner of a seat is underused before hiring a second person into it
Write a hire as the missing store function, never as a generic strong hire
Put a planning/ops owner in place before the first demand surge
Name a backup for every key artefact, login and supplier relationship (key-person risk)
Run an org-chart-vs-revenue-stage review every quarter
Give marketplace and subscription channels their own named owner, separate from DTC silos
Audit for one person carrying too much of the store's decisions and build a second path
inputs: brand brain: org chart, revenue history
founder_sees: Whether the org is sized right for the current revenue, and who the store cannot afford to lose.

name: Build hiring scorecards and run structured hiring
what: Build a structured job description (silo, artefacts, metric), an honest job ad, a sourced interview question set and comp bands before a search opens, and score candidates on scorecard behaviors, not channel skill alone.
encompasses: Write a structured job description naming silo, artefacts and the seat's metric
Write the job ad honest and demanding about the real workload
Set comp bands for the role before opening the search
Use a sourced interview question set, not an invented rubric
Score a candidate on whether they will flag a bad brief out loud
Screen every hire for self-directed drive and brand-values fit, not competence alone
Look for talent past the org chart before an external search
Debate internal promotion vs external hire openly, then have the leader decide with a stated criterion
inputs: brand brain: role library, comp bands
founder_sees: A ready-to-run hiring pack: role, ad, interview questions and a scorecard.

name: Write onboarding and standard operating procedures
what: Write and keep current the SOPs a new hire needs in week 1 (the live operating artefacts, not just team norms), and give every operating artefact one named owner with a fixed update cadence.
encompasses: Walk every new hire through the live operating artefacts in week 1
Give every operating artefact one named owner and a fixed update cadence
Draft a new SOP when a procedure has repeated 3 times (send to founder for review before use)
inputs: brand brain: existing SOPs, artefact list
trigger: event: new hire or repeated procedure
founder_sees: A week-1 onboarding pack and one place that lists who owns every recurring document.

name: Design the weekly and quarterly management rhythm
what: Design and maintain the store's meeting cadence (annual reset, quarterly deep dive, weekly trading review, ad hoc), a visible scoreboard, and cascading messaging, sized to a small brand.
encompasses: Run 4 meeting types at a small-brand length: annual, quarterly, weekly, ad hoc
Run the weekly meeting on the jugular numbers, cancel it when there is nothing to debate
Publish every goal, owner and standard where the whole team can see it
Run cascading messaging in the last 10 minutes of every staff meeting
Set 2 meeting ground rules and defend them against pushback
Prune recurring reports and channels that have become communication sludge
Book the post-peak check-in before the peak starts
Audit a recurring meeting each quarter against known traits of an effective team
Match communication method to work type: live meetings for interdependent work, dashboards for routine work
founder_sees: A meeting calendar sized to the brand, plus the scoreboard everyone sees.

name: Run team trust, accountability and decision facilitation guides
what: Prepare structured facilitation guides (team dysfunction assessment, trust exercises, conflict and accountability tools) for the founder to run with the team, tied every quarter to one real store metric.
encompasses: Prepare the quarterly team dysfunction assessment and pair the score with one real metric
Prepare trust-building exercises (personal histories, team effectiveness, strength/weakness rounds)
Prepare conflict-facilitation guides (conflict-style read, force field analysis, role negotiation)
Prepare accountability guides (natural consequences, proposed-fix requirement, effort-based accountability)
Flag a destructive high performer or fit issue for the founder with the evidence, never act on it directly
Prepare a root-cause check for a missed launch (communication, structural, personal)
Prepare a departure communication and same-day interim-owner plan
founder_sees: A ready-to-run guide for the founder's next team session, tied to a real number.

name: Evaluate and manage vendors, 3PLs and agencies
what: Run vendor and 3PL selection by competitive RFP with a facility visit, put SLAs in writing with a stated consequence for a miss, audit every invoice against the brand's own order volume in code, and set scope, cost and review owner before any agency pod starts.
encompasses: Choose a 3PL by competitive RFP with a facility visit, never one quote
Put the 3PL SLA in writing with a pick-time clause and a stated consequence for a miss
Track delivered-on-time directly and split pick lag from carrier lag before claiming a credit
Audit every monthly 3PL invoice against the brand's own order volume in code
Re-shop freight providers monthly, compare 2-3 at a time
Set scope, cost and review owner before adding any agency pod or contractor roster
Give a 3PL the growth forecast the brand actually intends to hit, not an inflated one
Send an advance shipping notice ahead of every inbound delivery
Decide fulfilment make-vs-buy before running a 3PL RFP
outputs: invoice audit report with overcharge flags
founder_sees: A scorecard on every vendor and 3PL, and any invoice that overcharged.

name: Govern supplier purchase orders and production
what: Gate large purchase orders on a documented tech pack, run a critical path with one owner and one date per production step, and route supplier communication through one channel kept as dispute evidence.
encompasses: Never release a large PO without a tech pack on file
Pick one negotiation lever per SKU: low MOQ, low price, or short lead time
Run a critical path with one owner and one date per step; never give suppliers edit access
Build the demand forecast base excluding stockout days, using a trend or seasonal curve
Set an inventory buffer policy by volatility and capital
Keep one authoritative PO copy in accounting software and one team-visible tracker
Route all supplier communication through one channel kept as dispute evidence
Agree refund and quantity-tolerance terms before wiring a large supplier payment
Decide supplier co-development vs an independent designer before sourcing
Flag that a sourcing edge is not a permanent moat
founder_sees: Whether a purchase order is safe to release, and the schedule that keeps it on time.

name: Plan customer-service capacity and ticket routing
what: Staff CS tiers from the sales forecast curve, track cost per ticket, define what counts as a complex ticket before routing it, and trace a rising resolution time upstream before blaming agents.
encompasses: Staff CS tiers from the sales forecast curve, track cost per ticket monthly
Staff a pre-purchase support lane for a considered or high-AOV product
Trace a rising resolution time upstream before blaming CS agents
Define what counts as a complex ticket before routing to new or offshore agents
Fix the PDP or size guide for a recurring pre-purchase question instead of answering it faster
Give the fulfilment owner the job of keeping purchase emotion alive after checkout
founder_sees: How many CS staff and tiers the current and forecast order volume actually needs.

name: Audit tooling and match it to revenue stage
what: Audit the store's software and tooling spend against its revenue stage (never an ERP too early), name a tracker owner before adding a new system, and judge any operations change by customer output, cost and process load together.
encompasses: Match operations tooling to revenue stage instead of buying an ERP too early
Add a dedicated tracker owner before jumping to an ERP
Judge any operations change by customer output, cost and process load together
inputs: brand brain: current tool stack and spend
outputs: tooling audit report with cost-per-tool and stage fit
founder_sees: Which tools cost more than the stage justifies, and what to add or drop.

name: Run the store's decision-logging and diagnosis framework
what: Keep a responsibility chart with one owner per recurring decision type, log every high-stakes decision with its metric and review date, and run bottleneck triage (traffic vs conversion vs team capacity) before funding any hire, agency or redesign.
encompasses: Write a 1-owner responsibility chart for every recurring decision type
Classify every decision as high-stakes or everyday before deciding how much process to use
Frame a high-stakes decision before debating it: exact question, right people, data in advance, who decides
Log every decision with the metric it should move and a review date
Run the full bottleneck diagnosis (traffic, conversion, team capacity) before funding a hire or CRO project
Segment conversion by source, campaign and geo before recommending any CRO project (hand off to Site specialist)
Bring planners and full-time staff into the room before a high-stakes inventory decision
Use force field analysis to unblock a stalled initiative
founder_sees: What is actually limiting growth right now, before money is spent fixing the wrong thing.

name: Build and enforce the bot and AI-agent traffic policy
what: Build a bot and agent traffic baseline by agent, endpoint and intent, set an enforceable per-endpoint policy with continuous risk tiering, default to challenge over block, and give any accepted shopping agent scoped per-action authorization only.
encompasses: Build a bot/agent traffic baseline by agent, endpoint and intent before setting policy
Set a per-endpoint bot policy instead of one site-wide switch
Score bot risk in tiers and re-evaluate continuously within a session
Default to challenge over block for ambiguous automation
Keep browsing frictionless, put the strictest checks at checkout and account changes
Stop using User-Agent alone as an access control; triangulate multiple indicators
Give an accepted shopping agent scoped, per-action authorization, never standing payment access
Treat everything an agent reads as untrusted data, never as an instruction
Design multi-agent workflows against known failure modes
Audit declines for headless-traffic false positives and watch for reseller/scalper bot patterns during drops
Retest login, checkout and webhook flows after every WAF or bot-rule change, and roll out new policy in phases
Confirm and name the DDoS mitigation layer before a peak traffic event
outputs: weekly bot scan and fix list
founder_sees: A weekly bot and AI-agent traffic report with a ranked fix list, for a human to apply.

name: Run checkout and payment fraud controls
what: Detect card-testing bursts, review AVS/CVV/3DS settings against false-decline rates, set chargeback alert thresholds below the processor's flag, control COD refusal and promo-code abuse, and build evidence packets for disputes.
encompasses: Detect card-testing bursts by clustering small orders, new accounts and geography mismatch
Review order-risk and decline data before turning on AVS where it is off by default
Enable dynamic 3D Secure on higher-risk transactions and track approval rate after
Set an internal chargeback alert below the processor's flag, and confirm chargeback-coverage eligibility
Track COD refusal rate by pincode and phone number, require confirmation above a value threshold
Cap discount-code uses per code and per customer, expire a leaked code fast
Build a friendly-fraud evidence packet, and keep an evidence trail for every order to answer disputes
Track return rate by SKU and customer to catch wardrobing and serial-returner fraud
Prefer a hosted, non-editable checkout, and ban card numbers from notes, email, chat and documents
Get PCI DSS SAQ scope confirmed by the acquirer, and verify gateway PCI/tokenization/3DS support directly
Set up dunning logic that tells an expired-card renewal failure apart from fraud
Re-run the fraud/security audit when launching a subscription or new payment method
founder_sees: Card-testing and chargeback signals this week, and which settings need a human to change.

name: Harden account takeover and authentication defenses
what: Audit login, session and multi-factor authentication design: 2FA/passkeys for admins, session-cookie attributes, password hashing and rate limiting, enumeration prevention, and risk-based step-up, with recovery designed before enforcement.
encompasses: Require 2FA with passkeys on every admin account, ranking second factors and enrolling hardware/passkeys first
Decide the account recovery path before enforcing strong second factors
Remove knowledge-based security questions as authentication factors
Set Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path and a bounded expiry on every session cookie, with high-entropy session IDs
Set a password policy of long and unique, breach-checked, no forced rotation
Hash any custom-login password with a maintained adaptive hasher and per-user salt
Rate-limit login, signup and reset per username and per IP
Return identical error messages and timing for wrong password vs no such user
Trigger step-up authentication on new device, new country, or many accounts from one source
Require re-authentication before changing email, password, payment method or payout details
Run quarterly phishing simulation training covering email, voice and SMS
Allow password paste and a password manager, and offer passwordless passkey login to customers
founder_sees: Which admin accounts and login flows are weak, and the exact setting to change.

name: Audit and fix web application security defects
what: Audit storefront and checkout code for XSS, injection, CSRF, clickjacking, CORS and postMessage defects, and produce a developer fix list requiring parameterised queries, output escaping, method-scoped routing and a 2-approver code review gate.
encompasses: Escape every user-rendered field by context using the framework's auto-escaping layer
Replace concatenated SQL/shell commands with parameterised queries and argument arrays
Add a stateless CSRF token and convert state-changing actions from GET to POST
Deny framing on checkout, cart, account and admin pages
Allow-list the Origin header on checkout and payment-method endpoints
Check both sides of any postMessage call before trusting the data
Replace JSONP with a CORS endpoint or server-side proxy
Add rel=noopener to every outbound target=_blank link
Serve the entire site over HTTPS, not only login and checkout
Require code review with at least 2 approvers, never edit the live theme
Stream large file downloads instead of buffering them in memory
Validate the Host header and bind to loopback on any local admin/sync tool
inputs: warehouse: site source (read, custom platform only)
founder_sees: A prioritized list of code-level security defects with the exact fix, for a developer.

name: Audit third-party scripts, apps and dependencies
what: Keep a live inventory of every app, theme, script, tag and dependency with owner and last use, vet new scripts before they are added, run automated CVE scanning, and review app permissions quarterly.
encompasses: Keep a live inventory of every app, theme, plugin and dependency with owner and last use
Vet a third-party script's access and privileges before adding it anywhere on the site
Lock dependency versions, review new direct dependencies, check names for typosquats
Run installs only in a disposable, network-restricted build environment
Read changelogs before updating; subscribe to platform and app security bulletins
Audit browser extensions on every admin, fulfilment and support machine
Run automated dependency vulnerability (CVE) scanning on every build
Rescore every disclosed vulnerability against the brand's own deployment
Inventory every third-party tag and script with vendor, purpose and consent status
Audit ad and analytics tags for fingerprinting; remove any the brand cannot justify
Change default credentials and update firmware on store network devices
Review app permissions quarterly and after adding any checkout, payment or customer-data app
founder_sees: Every app, script and dependency the store runs, who owns it, and any risky permission.

name: Review admin access and least-privilege roles
what: Map every staff role to only the admin areas it needs, run a full staff access audit with same-day offboarding, monitor admin logins for new locations or devices, and issue automation credentials as revocable, scoped, logged records.
encompasses: Map every staff role to only the admin areas it needs, revoke access outside it
Restrict and alert on admin logins from new locations, devices or times
Issue every automation credential as a revocable, scoped, logged record
Run a full staff access audit with a same-day offboarding process
inputs: brand brain: staff roster and roles
founder_sees: Who has access to what in the admin, and any access that no longer matches the role.

name: Maintain backups and the incident response runbook
what: Run daily versioned backups to 3 separated locations with a ransomware-safe copy, test restores end to end, and maintain a unified incident runbook covering breach, skimming, account takeover and ransomware together.
encompasses: Run daily versioned backups to 3 separated locations, one ransomware-safe, tested for restore
Log admin, order-risk, automation-flow and DNS/header changes, with someone assigned to act
Scan storefront files for malware on a schedule; treat any detection as a breach until proven otherwise
Treat unexplained changes to shipping address, order contents or payment routes as compromise signals
Follow a fixed sequence on a skimming signal: offline, remove, rotate, check, notify
Lock or flag customer accounts and force resets after any breach touching the customer base
Build the incident runbook to handle chargebacks, fines and churn together, not as separate tracks
Run a full restore test end to end, not just confirm backups exist
founder_sees: Proof the last backup can actually be restored, and the runbook to follow if something breaks.

name: Monitor domain, DNS and brand-impersonation risk
what: Lock the domain registrar account, audit DNS for dangling records, and watch for lookalike domains, counterfeit marketplace listings and Safe Browsing blocklist flags against the brand.
encompasses: Lock the domain registrar account and audit DNS for dangling records
Watch for lookalike and IDN homograph domains impersonating the brand
Watch marketplaces and social ads for counterfeit listings using the brand's name and photos
Monitor Safe Browsing status for the storefront domain
inputs: brand brain: domain and DNS records
founder_sees: Any lookalike domain, counterfeit listing or blocklist flag found this week.

name: Audit privacy, consent and tracking compliance
what: Confirm GDPR/CCPA exposure by customer location, publish a privacy policy covering AI-agent interactions with a compliant consent banner, and remove non-payment third-party tags from checkout.
encompasses: Confirm GDPR/CCPA exposure by customer location; keep the fine and notification duty visible
Publish a privacy policy covering AI agent interactions and run a compliant consent banner
Never reuse a contact detail collected for 2FA or receipts for retargeting without separate consent
Remove non-payment third-party tags from the checkout and payment step
Re-verify current browser cookie/tracking defaults before building any measurement plan
Never repurpose HSTS as a tracking mechanism
Run a full privacy and consent check across storefront, account and checkout pages
founder_sees: Whether the store's privacy and consent setup matches the law where its customers are.

name: Run the quarterly security audit program
what: Run the recurring four-pillar security audit with a named owner per pillar, confirm platform SOC/PCI claims before repeating them, maintain the hosted-vs-self-hosted responsibility map, and run a full threat model and vulnerability disclosure program.
encompasses: Run a quarterly four-pillar security audit with a named owner per pillar
Triage a security finding by whether a working exploit exists, not by its label
Write down which security duties the hosted platform covers vs the merchant
Confirm what a platform's SOC 1/SOC 2 audit actually covers before citing it
Verify Shopify's (or the platform's) default security claims against current documentation
Build a full store threat model weighted by peak calendar, region and past incidents
Publish a vulnerability disclosure channel with a stated response and fix SLA
Build a quarterly security review calendar covering every checklist and its owner
inputs: brand brain: platform, past incidents, peak calendar
founder_sees: The quarterly security scorecard: what was checked, what failed, and who owns the fix.

name: Mine reviews for avatar and language signals
what: Read the brand's own product reviews by star band and pull identity markers, struggle language, objections and repeated words the avatar record and copy can use.
encompasses: Pull all reviews per SKU with star rating and date
Read 1 and 2 star reviews for the real objection, not the surface complaint
Read 4 and 5 star reviews for the job the product actually did
Scan for identity markers like 'I am a' or 'as a'
Prioritize long narrative reviews over short generic ones
Discount single contradictory reviews, act only on repeated patterns
Capture every usable quote verbatim with source and date
Flag use cases no competitor targets
outputs: tagged quote set by star band
founder_sees: Kevin sees a short list of what customers actually said, sorted by how often it repeats, with the exact quotes.

name: Mine support tickets, returns and calls for struggle language
what: Read support tickets, return reasons and call transcripts as passive evidence of the customer's real struggle, separate from anything they said to make a sale.
encompasses: Pull tickets, return reasons and call transcripts for the period
Tag each by the underlying job or failure, not the surface request
Cluster repeated complaint patterns
Feed named objections into standing support macros
Flag sizing, fit or fulfilment anxieties for the avatar record
Log consent status before any quote leaves the ticket system
founder_sees: Kevin sees the real reasons people struggle or return, in their own words, not a guess.

name: Run forum and social listening research
what: Search public forums, Reddit, Quora and social platforms in the avatar's own words to find language, objections and sub-avatars a review file would miss.
encompasses: Search forums using the avatar's own words, not marketing language
Read comments on a thread, not only the original post
Use Reddit for emotional language and Quora for tactics, verified per category
Cross-check search interest terms against buying behavior
Map mass, niche and sub-avatar layers from social content
Confirm platform choice with real demographic data, not a guess
inputs: connector: social listening tool if available
founder_sees: Kevin sees what real people say about this category in public, in their own words, with the source link.

name: Mine on-site search and behavior for job clues
what: Read the brand's own on-site search terms and browse-without-buy sessions for what shoppers were actually trying to find.
encompasses: Pull on-site search query logs and no-result searches
Pull browse-without-buy session paths
Match queries to existing or missing product jobs
Flag a repeated no-result query as a possible product or content gap
founder_sees: Kevin sees what shoppers searched for and did not find.

name: Design and run customer interview programs
what: Write the interview guide, pick the channel and incentive, and run or hand off real conversations with customers to hear the job in their own words.
encompasses: Book a standing weekly slot for calls or DMs
Frame every invite as exploratory, never as sales or support
Match the incentive to the person, never cash to a high earner
Ask about the situation and struggle, never features, color or price
Cover every comparison step for a considered purchase
Log consent and storage location for every quote
Treat 1 interview as 1 data point; cluster several before changing a record
Extend interview timeline coverage for slow, considered purchases
Use a lightweight email or DM reply when a call is not possible
founder_sees: Kevin gets a ready interview guide and a place to log calls; the agent never talks to customers on his behalf without him agreeing to the plan.

name: Design and field customer surveys
what: Write short, targeted surveys, identity, post-purchase or NPS, to confirm what research found at wider scale, never to discover a new job.
encompasses: Write a short first-party identity survey for existing customers
Write a post-purchase or verification survey to confirm findings, run after interviews not before
Design a segmenting question for a pop-up in place of an instant discount
Run NPS quarterly, segmented by historical customer value
Run research separately with complaining and non-complaining customers
Cap the share of budget spent on collecting more data versus acting on it
founder_sees: Kevin gets a survey ready to send and a plain-language summary of what came back.

name: Research competitors and public benchmarks for avatar and positioning signals
what: Read competitor ads, pages, reviews and Q&A as public signal only, never as private data, to map the mainstream avatar, screen angles and check market health.
encompasses: Map the mainstream avatar from the Meta Ad Library
Read competitor headlines for the constraint and reward they encode
Use ad duration as a screening signal only, never proof of a winning angle
Search the Ad Library for a candidate angle before committing to it
Read competitor page polish as a market-health signal
Use a competitor demographic lookup as a cold-start seed when no avatar exists
Compare review counts across listings as a rough demand proxy
Score the brand and competitors on real category attributes
founder_sees: Kevin sees what competitors show in public, marked as signal only, never as something to copy.

name: Run AI-assisted deep research with quote verification
what: Use AI deep research as a second pass after a manual sprint, on one prioritized candidate at a time, and verify every quote at its original source before it enters a record.
encompasses: Complete one manual research sprint before running AI deep research
Run the AI report on 1 prioritized candidate at a time
Verify every quote the AI surfaces at its real source
Let AI draft the avatar record from first-party transcripts, then verify every claim
Reject any AI-drafted line that cannot be traced to a real source
