founder_sees: Kevin sees which product format and packaging fit a new channel before he commits to it.

name: Advise founder operating practices for brand-building
what: Turn recurring brand-building operating patterns, hiring sequence, ideation method, decision speed and readiness checks, into short, reusable guidance for the founder and team.
encompasses: Screen hires for lean execution autonomy, not resume pedigree
Hire generalists early, then narrow specialists as revenue scales
Treat decision and response speed as the small brand's real competitive edge
Check for real resources and stamina before starting a demanding brand initiative
Run naming or creative ideation in individuals or 2-person teams, not large groups
Separate idea generation from evaluation in every ideation session
Force clear high or low scores on candidates; ban the middle
Generate candidates through 3 different information lenses
Judge early-stage content or product work by craft, not early metrics
Screen investors for operator experience and behavior, not just check size
founder_sees: Kevin gets short, practical notes on how to hire, decide and ideate at this stage, not a generic playbook.

name: Run the weekly business review
what: Roll up the metric contract, the top bottleneck, what shipped last week, and what is due this week into one weekly view the founder reads in under 5 minutes. Matches how a fractional CMO opens the week with a data pass before directing the team.
encompasses: pull the metric contract and flag anything unavailable, never zero
list what each specialist shipped or is blocked on since the last review
surface the one number that moved most and why, in plain words
carry forward open founder decisions from the decision log
flag any registry read point due this week
note any metric outside its normal band for 2+ weeks running
outputs: list of decisions needed this week
founder_sees: One page: the number that moved, what shipped, what needs a decision.

name: Teach the founder to question a number before acting on it
what: Before a bottleneck, a claim, or a competitor's headline is used to justify a decision, run it through a short skepticism check and show the founder the check, not just the conclusion. Builds founder judgment over time instead of just handing down verdicts.
encompasses: 3-question check on any growth claim before it enters a proposal
flag when a metric change lags a real event (platform attribution window change, seasonal spike)
explain why a bottleneck was or was not confirmed, in the founder's own numbers
distinguish measured, source-claimed and general-practice basis on every idea shown
log which explanations the founder found useful, to reuse the framing
outputs: short explainer attached to each proposal card
trigger: event: a claim or ranked idea reaches the founder
founder_sees: A one-line reason why a number can or cannot be trusted yet.

name: Allocate budget across channels, not inside one
what: Decide how much of the next dollar goes to Meta, Google, email, organic and creators, before any specialist decides how to spend their own slice. Built bottom-up from each channel's own headroom, not a fixed percent template.
encompasses: read each channel's own frontier (headroom before returns drop) from its specialist
scale the primary channel to its named headroom before funding a new one
strip one-off inflators before comparing channels
coordinate paid spend against the owned calendar (email, organic pushes)
recommend a next-best-dollar split with the reasoning shown
flag when a channel's spend has drifted from the last agreed split
inputs: metric contract: spend and return by channel
founder_sees: Where the next dollar should go and why, with a number behind each channel.

name: Run a launch playbook that spans channels
what: When a new product, market or brand launches, sequence the specialists in the right order (validation, then flows, then paid, then content) instead of letting each one start independently. One launch, one plan, several specialists executing against it.
encompasses: stage demand validation cheaply before any paid spend is approved
require welcome and abandoned-cart flows live before paid scales
sequence pre-launch anticipation, a hype-channel test, then list building
assign each launch step to its owning specialist with a date
hold a single launch timeline the founder can see end to end
roll learnings from one launch into the next one's plan
founder_sees: One launch calendar with every specialist's part and date on it.

name: Keep the seasonal calendar (India festivals, wedding season, sales events)
what: Hold the year's fixed demand and cost windows (Diwali, wedding season, Q4 Western peak, Republic Day and other sale events) and push each specialist's prep deadline backward from them, so budget, creative and inventory are ready before the window, not during it.
encompasses: hold the dated calendar of festival, wedding-season and sale windows relevant to the brand's market
write the full peak plan at least 70 days before a major window
set base and stretch budget gates with numeric triggers ahead of each window
decide the window's objective (profit play or inventory play) before spend starts
remind each specialist of its pre-window deadline (creative volume, page load, stock)
protect evergreen spend and flows from being cut for the sale window
run the post-window read separately (peak-launch attribution needs its own correction)
trigger: continuous, with named milestones ahead of each window
founder_sees: The next dated window, what is ready, and what is not, with time to fix it.
gap_note: The bank's peak-season ideas are written for a generic Western Q4 (Black Friday, holiday). Nothing in the bank names Diwali, Indian wedding season or India-specific sale calendars (Republic Day, end-of-season sale) by date. This calendar has to be built from the brand brain and general web research, not the bank.

name: Run the crisis response protocol
what: For a stockout, a negative-press event, a platform ban or account suspension, or a death-spiral metric pattern, assemble the right specialists fast, hold one message to the founder, and keep a single response timeline instead of each specialist reacting alone.
encompasses: detect the trigger pattern (CAC and volume diverging, a account restriction, a stock-out on a hero SKU, a viral complaint)
assemble a named cross-functional response group within 24 hours
hold one source of truth for what happened and what is being done
route the founder to the one decision only they can make
keep a transparent, factual update cadence instead of going silent
log the incident and the response in the decision log for the post-mortem
stand down the crisis mode and confirm normal operating resumes
inputs: brand brain: current crisis, if any
founder_sees: What broke, who is on it, and the one call only the founder can make.

name: Set and track goals (OKRs) for the quarter
what: Turn the founder's stated priority into a small set of measurable objectives and key results, tied to the metric contract, and check them weekly so the loop's daily proposals stay pointed at what the founder actually asked for.
encompasses: translate a founder priority into 1 to 3 objectives with 3 to 5 measurable key results each
tie every key result to a metric contract field, never a made-up number
check key results weekly, not just at quarter end
flag when the ranked proposal list is not moving the stated objective
run a quarterly stage review against measurement, creative, structure and team
close the quarter with a plain-language read: hit, missed, why
founder_sees: 3 goals for the quarter, each with a number, checked every week.

name: Hold the experiment design standard
what: Give every approved idea the same shape of test before a specialist runs it: a named metric, a read point sized to reach real signal, and a kill and scale rule agreed before the result comes in. Stops both premature kills and endless tests.
encompasses: size the read point to the metric's own noise, not a fixed day count (60 to 180 days for slow metrics, days for fast ones)
write the kill and scale rule before the test starts, not after the result
record a pre-change baseline with a timestamp for every structural change
treat every idea's expected effect as a hypothesis until the brand's own data confirms it
flag a test that is too small to reach its own read point
standardise how confidence and basis (measured, source-claim, general-practice) are shown to the founder
inputs: prior test history for this idea
outputs: test design attached to every registry entry
founder_sees: Every test comes with its own finish line, agreed up front.

name: Rank candidates without letting the loudest source win
what: Score every candidate idea, whether from the bank, the brand's own audit, or the web, on the same formula (reach, effect, effort, cost, risk, confidence, founder weight) so a well-evidenced web idea can outrank a weak bank idea and a weak bank idea can be demoted with a stated reason.
encompasses: compute reach, effect, effort, cost, risk and confidence in code from the brand's own numbers
apply founder weights learned from past approve or reject reasons
never let source (bank vs audit vs web) count as a scoring factor on its own
state in plain words why a candidate was demoted or promoted
fix the one binding constraint before ranking secondary ones
surface dependencies between candidates before ranking them independently
move fast on internal, reversible bets; slow down and gate anything customer-facing
inputs: candidate list from bank, audit and web
outputs: ranked proposal list with stated reasons
trigger: event: a diagnose run produces candidates
founder_sees: A ranked list where the reason for the order is written next to each item.

name: Keep the decision log
what: Record every founder approve, reject or park decision with its stated reason, once, and turn repeated reasons into ranking weights instead of asking the founder to repeat themselves on the next similar idea.
encompasses: capture the founder's exact reason at the moment of approve, reject or park
tag the reason to the idea's attributes (bottleneck, cost, risk, channel)
turn a repeated reason into a standing ranking weight
surface the decision log so a new proposal does not repeat a rejected pattern without saying so
run a would-we-approve-it-again check in every post-mortem
keep the log queryable by specialist and by brand for the review page
inputs: founder decision on a proposal card
trigger: event: a founder decision is made
founder_sees: Nothing extra to do; their reasons quietly shape future rankings.

name: Write the board and investor update
what: Turn the metric contract, the quarter's approved and executed ideas, and the founder's own notes into a short investor or board update in the standard shape: headline number, wins with numbers, what did not work, asks.
encompasses: pull the headline metric and 2 to 3 numeric wins from the metric contract and registry
state what did not go as planned and what was learned, not just wins
list hires, org changes and anything affecting execution
write a specific ask (introduction, advice, resource) if the founder has one
keep the same structure every period so readers can scan it fast
never invent a number; missing data shows as unavailable
founder_sees: A drafted update ready to send, in a template that stays the same each time.

name: Run the pre-delivery integrity gate
what: Before any specialist's output reaches the founder, check that arithmetic ran in code, totals stay separate from breakdowns, missing data shows as unavailable, and tracking exclusions are correct, so a bad number never becomes the basis for a decision.
encompasses: recompute every number in the deliverable from source, never trust a stated figure
confirm missing or blocked data is marked unavailable, not shown as zero
check that a spend, creative or budget call has clean tracking underneath it (bot traffic, internal traffic excluded)
confirm windows end on a full day, not a partial one
check that no competitor text, logo, product or face was copied
block delivery and name the fix needed if a check fails
outputs: pass or fail with named fixes
trigger: event: any specialist output is ready to deliver
founder_sees: Only output that already passed the checklist; failures never reach them.

name: Run the competitor and reference intake standard
what: Give every competitor teardown the same structure, whether it feeds a specialist's brief or the reference library, so patterns are separated from noise before anyone acts on them.
encompasses: classify a competitor account as creating demand or harvesting an existing one
map competitor creative to a fixed format and script taxonomy
audit a competitor's proof numbers and P&L claims for internal consistency before trusting them
separate what is transferable to this brand from what is not, and say why
audit where a competitor routes paid traffic and which pages get none
count concept diversity at peak season, not just asset count
tag every reference with structure and mood only, never text, logo, product or face to copy
outputs: tagged reference set with transferable-pattern notes
trigger: on demand, when a specialist requests references
founder_sees: References tagged with what is transferable and what is signal only.

name: Brief capital, exit and succession decisions
what: For a raise, a strategic partner, a sale process or a succession, assemble the numbers and the standard questions into one memo, since no specialist owns this surface and the founder should not face it with a blank page.
encompasses: write a capital and ownership memo with a downside case for every option on the table
verify claimed exit multiples against real comparables, never assume them
screen a strategic partner or minority-sale offer with the 1+1=3 test
interrogate deal terms and any buyer-imposed debt load before an offer is accepted
check accounting is audit-ready and transparent ahead of a sale process
define the successor archetype before a CEO succession hire is opened
time a due-diligence process around peak trading, not through it
choose an investment or acquisition partner on fit tested through real time together, not the term sheet alone
inputs: founder's stated intent (raise, partner, sale, succession)
trigger: event: founder opens a capital, partner, sale or succession question
founder_sees: One memo with the numbers, the downside case, and the standard questions already asked.

name: Diagnose the growth stage and archetype
what: Before ranking any fix, name what kind of growth problem the brand actually has (which channel, which layer, which archetype, which stage) so the right specialist and the right lever get engaged instead of the most familiar one.
encompasses: run the top-down root-cause order: business, channel, campaign type, campaign, submetric
run the 3-layer read (ads, funnel, backend) and the 2-signal read (creative vs funnel vs price)
name the brand's growth archetype before a lever is picked
detect the death-spiral pattern (CAC rising, volume falling, spend raised to compensate) as its own state
decide whether an underperformer is an angle problem or an offer problem
require 2 or more weak periods before treating a dip as a real bottleneck, not noise
match a confirmed bottleneck to founder hours, a hire, or a system change
trigger a full operating-foundation rebuild at a plateau instead of adding tasks
outputs: ranked bottleneck list with the archetype and stage named
founder_sees: The real bottleneck, named plainly, with the numbers that prove it.
